sources.title: Labor Surcharge and Equipment Rental Rates (Cost of Equipment Ownership) - Caltrans annual rate book, with FAQ
sources.owner: California Department of Transportation (Caltrans), Division of Construction
sources.data_provided: Statewide equipment rental rates by equipment class/make/model (an aggregator listing describes them as per-hour) plus the Caltrans labor surcharge (statutory employer payroll items). Used by Caltrans for force-account / change-order payment. Other edition files seen in results: book_26_27.pdf and book_26v3.pdf (same folder), and annual books back to 1998 at website.dot.ca.gov/hq/construc/eqrr/. A corrected .CSV of the rates is said to exist on the rental-rate website (per the Aug 2023 memo; CSV URL not seen).
sources.geography: California statewide (whether rates vary by district/region is NOT confirmed by snippets)
sources.period_covered: Edition-based. Search summaries conflict: book_26v3 cover = Apr 1 2026 to Aug 31 2026; book_26_27 and the FAQ = Apr 1 2026 to Mar 31 2027; book_26_27_intv2 = Sep 1 2026 to Mar 31 2027 (fuel-driven update). Historical editions 1998 onward.
sources.edition: As of 2026-10-24 the file book_26_27_intv2.pdf appears to be the latest (Sep 2026 interim update) - UNCONFIRMED; verify live page. Landing page URL (dot.ca.gov/programs/construction/equipment-rental-rates-and-labor-surcharge) is a derived pattern from the FAQ URL, not seen directly.
sources.access_notes: Per search summary: books are no longer available in hard copy and should be downloaded from the internet. PDF plus CSV. Caltrans also hosts an unofficial 'Dummy Rate Calculator' / equipment rental rate calculator at mets.dot.ca.gov for equipment not in the book. Rate requests for unlisted equipment go through the Caltrans field office (rental.rates@dot.ca.gov per summary). dot.ca.gov is blocked from the sandbox, so the PDFs were not opened.
sources.reuse_terms: Per search snippet, Caltrans sub-site terms state that nothing in the Site shall be construed as conferring any license under the Department's intellectual property rights; Caltrans global Conditions of Use page text was not retrieved. The rate book is a state-agency schedule published for contract use, but commercial redistribution/ingestion terms are unconfirmed.
sources.limitations: Contract force-account schedule, NOT a market rental rate (FAQ notes rental yards include overhead and profit and higher short-term costs). Rates assume contractor-owned equipment. Snippets list fuel, oil/lube, repairs, depreciation, facilities capital, insurance as included; whether operator labor is excluded is NOT stated in any snippet (see findings). Edition/period dates conflict across snippets.
sources.update_frequency: Annual book effective April 1, with interim updates (e.g., Aug/Sep 2026 interim edition tied to fuel cost); Aug 2023 memo shows corrections issued mid-year.
sources.evidence_quote: It says the diesel cost, from the book effective April 1, 2026, through March 31, 2027, is $4.85/gallon, which suggests a year-long period. The book cover says August 31, 2026, so the end date is unclear from these results.

sources.title: Caltrans Contract Cost Data (searchable historic bid results database)
sources.owner: California Department of Transportation (Office of Engineer / Division of Engineering Services)
sources.data_provided: Item-level historic bid results: item number and description, bid opening date, district-county-route-postmile, quantity, unit price, total price. Search returns average unit cost, standard deviation and total price. Includes non-awarded bids (help text tells users to review non-awarded outliers). Item-code lookup page exists (codes.php); latest item code list is available from HQ as an MS Word file. Same app is mirrored on district hosts (d8data.dot.ca.gov).
sources.period_covered: Third-party scraper listing claims 1993-2025; Caltrans pages seen with record count 3,412,387 and latest bid-open date imported 03-04-2026 (one snapshot) and 04-30-2026 (another snapshot).
sources.edition: Live database; snapshots differ in import date
sources.access_notes: No official bulk download/export or API is described in any snippet. Unaffiliated Apify scrapers advertise CSV/JSON/Excel extraction of this database - their legality under Caltrans conditions of use is unverified; do not scrape without confirming terms. Site states use constitutes acceptance of conditions of use (text not retrieved). For newest bids Caltrans points to the HQ bid summary results page. Hosts are on dot.ca.gov (blocked from sandbox).
sources.reuse_terms: Per search snippet the site 'states that use of this site constitutes acceptance of the conditions of use'; the conditions text was not in results. No export or reuse license seen.
sources.limitations: BID PRICES (contract benchmark including contractor overhead, profit, market conditions), not installed cost or productivity. Caltrans advises: use at least 20 results, limit to district and nearby districts, keep quantity range within about an order of magnitude, large quantities bid lower, check standard deviation vs average. Highway/bridge/civil items (concrete, rebar, demolition, paving, signs) - little building-trade coverage (framing, drywall, MEP).
sources.evidence_quote: Individual records show the item number and description, bid opening date, district-county-route-postmile, quantity, unit price, and total price.

findings.topic: Caltrans EQRR current edition and effective dates
findings.statement: Three Caltrans rate-book files were seen: book_26v3.pdf (cover: Apr 1 2026 to Aug 31 2026), book_26_27.pdf (Apr 1 2026 to Mar 31 2027) and book_26_27_intv2.pdf (reported as Sep 1 2026 to Mar 31 2027, fuel-driven update). The search summaries conflict on effective dates. As of 2026-10-24, book_26_27_intv2.pdf is the likely current edition. The effective period of every edition must be read from the live PDF cover before use. Books are revised each April 1 with interim updates.
findings.evidence_quote: The most recent edition found covers September 1, 2026 through March 31, 2027. That update was driven by higher fuel costs (it was published to update equipment rates based on current fuel costs).

findings.topic: Caltrans EQRR - what the rate includes (ownership vs operating)
findings.statement: Caltrans rates are ownership-based schedule rates assuming contractor-owned equipment. Components listed in the FAQ: major repair and overhaul, depreciation, facilities capital cost, fuel, oil and lube, field repair. Caltrans training slides add that the rate includes fuel, repairs and maintenance, supplies, small tools not consumed, necessary attachments, depreciation, insurance and incidentals. So Caltrans rates bundle ownership AND operating costs. Fuel is priced from a one-year average California weekly diesel price ($4.85/gal incl. taxes for the Apr 2026-Mar 2027 book; taxes removed for off-highway equipment).
findings.evidence_quote: The FAQ says some of the main components of the rate include major repair and overhaul, depreciation, facilities capital cost, fuel, oil and lube, and field repair costs.

findings.topic: Operator exclusion - Caltrans and USACE rates
findings.statement: No search snippet states whether operator wages are excluded from the Caltrans rate or from USACE EP 1110-1-8 rates. Belief from prior knowledge (UNVERIFIED): both schedules are equipment-only rates that exclude operator labor, which is paid separately (at Caltrans, as labor plus labor surcharge). The database should store these as equipment-only and must confirm against the PDFs before loading. Comparable evidence seen for another agency: a USDA Forest Service guide excludes operator rates (listed separately in its labor section) and includes fuel and maintenance in its equipment rates, and is Blue Book based.
findings.evidence_quote: The results don't say whether operator wages are excluded from the equipment rate.

findings.topic: Caltrans labor surcharge definition
findings.statement: The labor surcharge is a percentage add-on to wages covering six statutory employer payroll items: Workers' Compensation, Social Security, Medicare, Federal Unemployment, State Unemployment, State Training taxes. The general rate is an average across job classifications common to Caltrans projects (2002 edition wording). Per the current FAQ the varying component is workers' compensation, derived from WCIRB pure premium rates with a load factor. The current surcharge percentage was NOT found in any snippet. Under the 9-1.04 force-account markup, training slides state labor = labor surcharge plus 35% (wording garbled, unverified). Surcharge covers statutory items only - it is not a full labor burden (health, vacation, union benefits are not in this list).
findings.evidence_quote: The labor surcharge is meant to cover the employer payroll costs that contractors owe on their crews. Those six items are Workers' Compensation, Social Security, Medicare, Federal Unemployment, State Unemployment, and State Training taxes.

findings.topic: Caltrans EQRR machine-readable path
findings.statement: An Aug 2023 Caltrans memo said some rates in the PDF were incorrect and pointed users to a corrected .CSV on the rental-rate website, so a CSV version of the rate book exists. The CSV URL was not seen; it should be located on the Caltrans equipment-rental-rates page.
findings.evidence_quote: It said some of the rates in the current .PDF copy are incorrect, and pointed users to a corrected .CSV file on the rental rate website.

findings.topic: Caltrans EQRR is a contract schedule, not market rent
findings.statement: Caltrans FAQ states commercial rental yards include overhead, profit and higher short-term costs, so Caltrans rates are not comparable to quoted rental-yard prices. Rates for unlisted equipment come via the Caltrans field office or an unofficial 'Dummy Rate Calculator' needing new equipment list or sales price, net horsepower and approximate weight.
findings.evidence_quote: Caltrans' FAQ notes that rental yards have overhead and profit in their rates and they have higher costs for short-term rentals.

findings.topic: Caltrans Contract Cost Data - access and export
findings.statement: Caltrans Contract Cost Data is a web search database (sv08data.dot.ca.gov and district-host mirrors) with item-level bid results (including non-awarded bids). No official bulk export, API or download is described in any snippet. Unaffiliated Apify scrapers advertise CSV/JSON/Excel extraction; their use is legally unverified and should not be adopted without Caltrans conditions-of-use review. An item-code list is obtainable from HQ as an MS Word file (construction contract standards page).
findings.evidence_quote: On downloads, none of the results describe an official export feature on the Caltrans site. A third-party Apify scraper advertises CSV, JSON, and Excel export, but it is not Caltrans-affiliated

findings.topic: Caltrans Contract Cost Data - bid price vs cost, usage cautions
findings.statement: Records are bid prices (including losing bids), not cost. Caltrans warns that many unit prices vary by geographic area, that contractors often bid lower on large quantities, and that if the standard deviation exceeds the minimum or average unit price the average is unreliable. Any value loaded into the owl-tower database from this source must be tagged as a bid-price benchmark with district, quantity band and date.
findings.evidence_quote: If the standard deviation is greater than the minimum or average unit price, your average (weighted, escalated or not) is not going to be an accurate representation of a good unit price to use.

findings.topic: Caltrans annual Cost Data book (weighted averages)
findings.statement: A Riverside County engineer's estimate guide describes Caltrans 'Contract Cost Data' as prices by standard item code, weighted averages of low bidders' prices that vary by district. A separate search found no confirmation that an annual printed/PDF Cost Data book still exists. Attribution of this statement to the Riverside PDF is inferred from result ordering.
findings.evidence_quote: Caltrans Contract Cost Data summarizes prices by standard item code, and those prices are weighted averages of low bidders' prices that vary by district and location.

findings.topic: Caltrans production-rate / estimating guidance
findings.statement: No Caltrans-published production-rate guide, 'Standard Estimate' production table, or Construction Manual labor-output table was found. A Caltrans design memo lists RS Means and F.W. Dodge as the industry sources for standard production rates used in contract time planning, i.e., Caltrans itself relies on commercial cost books. Attribution of this sentence to the f0006218 PDF is inferred from result ordering. Caltrans Standard Specifications / Construction Manual text was not located (Section 9-1.04 content seen only through training slides).
findings.evidence_quote: A Caltrans design memo lists RS Means and F.W. Dodge publications as industry sources for standard production rates used in contract time planning.

findings.topic: Caltrans terms of use / reuse
findings.statement: No clear license covers the equipment rate book or Contract Cost Data. Observed: sub-site terms deny any implied IP license; Local Assistance publications may be downloaded, printed, distributed and copied but not modified; the 2026 CA MUTCD states its contents are not copyrighted. Global dot.ca.gov Conditions of Use page text was not retrieved. Treat rate book and Contract Cost Data as 'permission/terms unconfirmed' (public-agency data, intended for contractor use, but reuse not licensed in snippets).
findings.evidence_quote: Electronic versions of Caltrans Local Assistance publications are made available on this web site for downloading, printing, distribution and copying. However, modification of the publications provided on this Local Assistance web site is not authorized.

findings.topic: Caltrans bid results sources
findings.statement: Caltrans Office Engineer posts preliminary bid results within 20 minutes after each opening and a bid summary results page; bid books are viewed with the Project Bids (BIDS) software. Archived bid books exist as PDFs at ppmoe.dot.ca.gov/archived/ (2007-era examples).
findings.evidence_quote: Preliminary Bid Results are posted on the Caltrans website within 20 minutes after the bid opening.

findings.topic: ADOT bid data
findings.statement: ADOT posts item-level bid tabulations only for a short rolling window (four months after award per the Bid Tabulations page; approximately 90 days per the contractor FAQ), so history must be harvested going forward or requested via public records request. ADOT also offers the E2C2 Historical Unit Price tool but disclaims that the Bid History displayed is not a recommended unit price. As-read results give only totals. No ADOT equipment rental rate schedule or force-account rate document was found.
findings.evidence_quote: Its Bid Tabulations page says tabulations are available for four months after the State Transportation Award Date. Its contractor FAQ says after award, the bid tabs are posted publicly on the Contracts & Specifications website for approximately 90 days.

findings.topic: NDOT bid data
findings.statement: NDOT posts the detailed bid tabulation on its Public Portal after each bid opening and gives the bid-item-level Engineer's Estimate on request after bid opening; advertisements show only a value range (R1-R54). No NDOT average-unit-price report or historical unit price database was found. No NDOT equipment rate schedule was searched beyond the general bid-data queries.
findings.evidence_quote: The detailed bid tabulation report goes on the NDOT Public Portal once bids are opened

findings.topic: Southern California local-agency bid data
findings.statement: LA County Public Works publishes per-solicitation Bid Summary PDFs with line-item quantities, unit prices and engineer's estimate (best SoCal line-item source found). City of Gardena, City of Torrance, San Bernardino County and San Diego Unified post bid tabulation PDFs of varying detail. City of LA BOE: current results were not found; an older BOE document says bid results are available by phone and on the city website, and bid packages are free through LABAVN. No LA Metro, LAUSD or Riverside County bid-result pages and no Los Angeles/San Diego/Riverside open-data portal dataset of construction bid line items were found. San Diego County's 2019 solicitation mentions a catalog of construction tasks with preset unit prices (JOC-style).
findings.evidence_quote: Bid packages are free and available from Los Angeles City's Business Assistance Virtual Network (www.labavn.org).

findings.topic: Bid prices are not costs - cautions across agencies
findings.statement: Every DOT/agency bid dataset here records contract bid prices (contractor overhead, profit, market conditions, quantity effects) and sometimes non-awarded bids. ADOT disclaims its history as a recommended price; TxDOT's manual says average low-bid prices are a starting point needing engineering judgment; FHWA says historical bid data is the most common approach, mainly for minor items. Records must be tagged 'bid_price' rather than 'cost'.
findings.evidence_quote: the TxDOT manual notes that average low-bid prices should only be used as a starting point from which a more accurate unit bid price can be derived with good engineering judgment.

findings.topic: Other states' average bid price programs (reference models)
findings.statement: Free structured average-bid-price publications exist outside the target region: TxDOT (statewide and district, 3- and 12-month averages), Oregon DOT (spreadsheets from bid tabs), Oklahoma DOT (weighted average item prices by item, region, quarter; PDF), West Virginia DOT (annual PDF/XLS, 2022-2025 reports), South Dakota DOT (annual Bid Item Price Report PDF), City of Austin (48-month average unit bid price database, quarterly). Useful as schema models and national cross-checks only.
findings.evidence_quote: Austin, TX: Its Average Unit Bid Prices Database provides historic bid information by bid item number for the past 48 months. It is updated quarterly.

findings.topic: USACE EP 1110-1-8 structure, editions and availability
findings.statement: The schedule is published as 12 regional volumes plus methodology and checkrate software, biennial per a library catalog, with PDFs freely hosted on USACE sites (nww.usace.army.mil and publications.usace.army.mil). Region VII volumes seen: Nov 2009 (obsolete, superseded by 30 Nov 2011), Apr 2014, Nov 2016. A 12 August 2021 EP 1110-1-8 document is reported, so the Nov 2016 volumes are not necessarily the latest. The region-to-state assignment (which volume covers CA, AZ, NV) was NOT established by any snippet; it must be read from the pamphlet front matter. Operator treatment, fuel price basis and regional adjustment factors were also not confirmed. Standby = facilities capital + 25% of depreciation.
findings.evidence_quote: The schedule is published as 12 regional volumes plus checkrate calculation software.

findings.topic: USACE EP 1110-1-8 regulatory standing and use in contracts
findings.statement: Contract clauses cap equipment rates at the Corps regional manual for the work location; the pamphlet establishes predetermined rates under FAR 31.105; FHWA has described it as an acceptable source of equipment usage rates without modification. These support its use as a defensible public benchmark, though it is a government cost-reimbursement schedule, not market rent.
findings.evidence_quote: FHWA has described the schedule as an acceptable source of equipment usage rates without modification.

findings.topic: NAVFAC P-405 availability and age
findings.statement: NAVFAC P-405 exists and is freely downloadable from EverySpec as an October 1996 revision (earlier NAVDOCKS P-405, 1963). It contains labor tables (man-hours per work function) and equipment and manpower estimates for Seabee work functions. Trades covered, units, crew compositions and output values could not be verified from snippets. Standards are 30 years old and military-crew based, so use only as a legitimately free baseline, not as a current California productivity source.
findings.evidence_quote: It gives labor tables and equipment and manpower estimates for common Seabee work functions, and it is free to download there.

findings.topic: Free government labor-hour standards - overall assessment
findings.statement: Free government sources with person-hour tables exist but are old or unverified: NAVFAC P-405 (1996), joint TM 3-34.41 / NTRP 4-04.2.3 / MCRP 3-40D.12 (Oct 2021, approved for public release; table contents unverified), TM 5-301/5-304 AFCS (1990, facility-level man-hours), DTIC AD0666236 handbook (date not shown, likely decades old). No search result confirmed free current trade-level labor-hour tables for framing, drywall, painting, concrete finishing, rebar, demolition, HVAC, electrical or plumbing. Highway production-rate research (FHWA TA 5080.15, TxDOT HyPRIS, INDOT/Purdue, FDOT 1988) addresses highway items and contract-time methodology rather than building-trade crew outputs. Commercial books (RS Means, Dodge) remain the standard sources.
findings.evidence_quote: The closest match for per-unit labor data is a DTIC technical report, AD0666236, a handbook of performance and production of plant, equipment, and labor prepared for use in estimating construction costs.

findings.topic: FHWA production-rate method guidance
findings.statement: FHWA TA 5080.15 recommends production rates based on eight-hour crew days or per piece of equipment, and warns that rates from total quantity over total time come out low because they include startup, cleanup and interruptions. FHWA Federal Lands guidelines add adjusting to the project's actual workday. These are useful normalization rules for any productivity records we ingest.
findings.evidence_quote: Production rates developed by reviewing total quantities and total time are not recommended as they may result in misleading rates which tend to be low since they may include startup, cleanup, interruptions, etc.

findings.topic: Rental company public rates and automated-access terms
findings.statement: No major rental company was confirmed to publish a public rate sheet. Home Depot rates are per store with 4-hour, daily, weekly and 4-week blocks. Sunbelt's llms.txt references a website-use terms page and robots.txt and flags its media repository as not permitted for LLM training; United Rentals' US website terms (updated Feb 19, 2026) include a Section 3 Prohibited Uses whose text was not retrieved, and an older Canadian-French version restricts reproduction without written consent. The search did not return any explicit scraper/robot clause for any of the three, so automated-access permission is UNCONFIRMED and should be assumed restricted; no scraping was performed. Unofficial guides quote example prices but could not be attributed to a URL.
findings.evidence_quote: The terms also restrict copying site content: no part of the Site or any content may be reproduced, stored, retransmitted and so on without written consent. That language is from the French Canadian version, which is dated 2020.

findings.topic: Free installed-cost and benchmark datasets
findings.statement: No open DOE/LBNL/NREL dataset of installed costs for air-source heat pumps or insulation was found. Items found: NREL GHPsRUS (geothermal heat pump installation prices from surveys, 2013, CC BY 4.0); TECH Clean California working data sets (California heat pump water heater and HVAC installations with Total Project Cost, license unstated); NYSERDA HVAC contractor survey (47 contractor surveys, New York, practices rather than clear installed prices); a Consumer Reports / Rewiring America crowdsourced quote dataset (openness not confirmed). The SlabCalc IEEE DataPort concrete indices are derived from public bid tabs (tier E). Several DataPort/data.gov dataset licenses are not shown in snippets.
findings.evidence_quote: I found no open DOE, LBNL, or NREL dataset of installed costs for heat pumps or insulation, and nothing confirmed as public domain.

gaps: Caltrans EQRR: actual rate values, current labor surcharge percentage, definitive effective dates of book_26_27_intv2 vs book_26_27 vs book_26v3, whether rates vary by district/region, and whether the operator is excluded - requires opening the PDF/CSV (dot.ca.gov is blocked from this sandbox; a different environment or a human download is needed). The CSV URL was not seen.

Caltrans Contract Cost Data: official conditions-of-use text (sv08data help/terms) and any sanctioned bulk export or data request process; whether the Office of Engineer still publishes an annual Cost Data book. Needs reading the live conditions page or a written request to Caltrans.
Caltrans global 'Conditions of Use' (dot.ca.gov footer link) text and any statement covering datasets and rate books.
Caltrans Standard Specifications 2024 Section 9-1.04 (force-account equipment, labor surcharge and markup) and Construction Manual text not retrieved; markups were seen only in training slides.

USACE EP 1110-1-8: which regional volume covers California, Arizona and Nevada (must be read from the pamphlet's region map in the front matter, e.g., EP 1110-1-8_RV1-12.pdf), the latest edition year (2021 or later vs Nov 2016), operator inclusion/exclusion, fuel price basis, regional adjustment factors, and reuse terms (no distribution/copyright statement seen).
NAVFAC P-405: actual table contents (trades, units, crew compositions, daily outputs), the NAVFAC-hosted original, and the distribution statement. Needs download and read.
Joint TM 3-34.41 / NTRP 4-04.2.3 / MCRP 3-40D.12 (2021): whether it includes labor-hour or crew-production tables by trade - needs reading the PDF.

No free, current, trade-level labor-hour or crew-output source (framing, drywall, painting, concrete placing/finishing, rebar, demolition, HVAC, electrical rough-in, plumbing) was confirmed; likely requires licensed commercial data, contractor-supplied history, or Owl Tower's own job-cost records.

ADOT and NDOT equipment rental rate schedules or force-account rates were not found; ADOT/NDOT standard specifications (force-account sections, Blue Book adoption) need a direct check. ADOT and NDOT average-unit-price reports not found (only bid tabs/E2C2).

City of Los Angeles BOE, LA Metro, LAUSD and Riverside County: no current bid-result pages or datasets located; LA County Public Works bid-results index/landing page and archive depth also not located.
Open-data portals (data.lacity.org, LA County, San Diego, Riverside) were not found to host construction bid line-item datasets; a targeted portal search would be needed.

Rental companies: actual website-use / automated-access clauses for Sunbelt, United Rentals (Section 3) and Home Depot, and whether any publish usable public rate sheets; needs reading the live terms and robots.txt (no scraping done).

Open installed-cost datasets: no insulation dataset, no LBNL installed-cost dataset for HVAC found; TECH Clean California data license, period, format, geographic granularity unknown; NYSERDA and Consumer Reports/Rewiring America datasets' license/availability unconfirmed.
IEEE DataPort SlabCalc 26-metro record license not shown; whether the 26 metros include Los Angeles not shown.
blocked_or_unverifiable: All numeric facts and quotes come from WebSearch result summary text (a model-written summary of search hits), not from opening the documents; no page or PDF body was read. Quotes marked as evidence are literal text from those summaries, so wording like 'The search turned up' may precede them.

dot.ca.gov, bls.gov, sam.gov and similar hosts are blocked by the sandbox network policy; no Caltrans file (rate book PDF/CSV, Contract Cost Data pages, Standard Specifications) was opened or verified.

Conflicting statements across summaries about Caltrans edition effective dates (Apr 1 2026-Aug 31 2026; Apr 1 2026-Mar 31 2027; Sep 1 2026-Mar 31 2027) and ADOT bid-tab retention (four months vs approximately 90 days) remain unresolved.

Several attributions of a sentence to a specific URL are inferred from the order of results, not stated: Caltrans production-rate memo (f0006218 PDF), Caltrans Contract Cost Data weighted-average statement (Riverside County guide PDF), USACE 12 August 2021 document (RV1-12 PDF), Purdue JTRP 331 as the INDOT study, Torrance document-to-listing mapping.
